subject: Discovery follow-up: per-token targets & host comparison
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Murray <alice@nexacare.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery follow-up: per-token targets & host comparison

Hi Alice — thanks again for carving out time earlier. Quick recap + a few follow-ups from our discovery call so we can get you a tight pilot proposal: 

Summary of your usage profile (as we discussed)
- Primary product: patient triage assistant + summarization for clinician notes
- Expected steady-state: ~10–15M tokens / month in months 2–6
- Initial pilot (month 1): 2–4M tokens as we validate prompts and latency targets
- Latency SLOs: 200–300ms p50 for short prompts, 600ms p95 target for multi-turn flows

Budget & target pricing
- You mentioned an internal target of roughly $3k–5k / month for steady-state inference spend
- That equates to a target of approximately $20–$35 per 1M tokens (depending on whether the pilot volume ramps to 10M or 15M) — please confirm if that range is still accurate 

What we need from you to finalize a proposal
- Confirm the expected monthly token range for months 2–6 (10M vs 15M)
- Any required compliance artifacts up front (SOC 2, DPA, specific data retention limits)
- Clarify whether you prefer Hosted API (faster path) vs Dedicated pool (predictable unit cost) for pricing comparisons

Next steps from our side
- Ben will put together a short cost model showing unit $/1M under Hosted vs Dedicated vs an Open-hosting baseline (we’ll include OpenAI/Anthropic public price references and an estimate of open-model hosting unit cost) — I’ll ask him to attach the workbook and a one‑pager.
- If we’re aligned on target $/1M and compliance posture, we can scope a 30-day pilot with usage caps and a credit to get started.

Thanks — feel free to reply inline. Happy to jump back on a quick 20-min call later this week if useful.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: redwood_cost_workbook_v3.xlsx (cost model), host_comparison_onepager.pdf (one-page host vs OpenAI/Anthropic summary)

From: Alice Murray <alice@nexacare.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: per-token targets & host comparison

Thanks Laura — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Volume: our central forecast for months 2–6 is 12M tokens / month (conservative), but we could be at 18M if adoption in the pilot cohort is strong. For the pilot please price for a 3–4M month and then show the 12M and 18M steady-state scenarios.

2) Target budget: the $3k–5k figure is the initial procurement bucket for month-to-month SaaS spend; for long-term vendor selection the procurement team would prefer a $/1M target in the $18–$25 range. If Redwood can demonstrate predictable unit economics that land in that band vs OpenAI/Anthropic we’ll be in a good position to move to a short list.

3) Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is required; DPA + data residency notes would be helpful. For now Hosted API is acceptable, but we’ll evaluate Dedicated if the unit economics swing there.

Can Ben share the workbook with the 3 volume scenarios and the quick host-versus-open chart? If so we’ll review and set a follow-up.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alice

Alice Murray
Head of Product, NexaCare
alice@nexacare.io | +1 617-555-0114

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Murray <alice@nexacare.io>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: per-token targets & host comparison

Hi Alice — looping in Karthik (solutions) and attaching the workbook + one-pager Laura referenced. High-level notes and the benchmarking approach so you have context before digging into the spreadsheet: 

Benchmarking approach
- Public reference: we list current public per-1M token price references for OpenAI and Anthropic (where available) as a baseline for API access cost.
- Host/open-model proxy: for open models we model the unit cost at three levels: managed-host (fully managed service), reserved/dedicated capacity (committed GPUs + infra), and self-host (customer-managed). Each row in the workbook shows amortized GPU, storage, networking, and orchestration overheads.

Preliminary numbers (illustrative, see workbook for full calc)
- OpenAI / Anthropic (public API): ~$20–$30 per 1M tokens depending on model class and context window assumptions
- Open-model managed hosts (commercial hosts of open models): ~$8–$18 per 1M tokens (varies by quantization and batching)
- Redwood Hosted (our expected proposal for Pilot): we can hit ~$16–$22 per 1M for the pilot volumes given typical batching/caching and a small pilot credit; exact depends on prompt mixes and context lengths
- Redwood Dedicated (committed reserved capacity): we can structure a 12‑month reserved price that brings the steady-state to ~$10–$15 per 1M at 12–18M tokens / month, with a minimum commit.

Proposal options to discuss
1) Pilot (fastest): Hosted API pilot, 3–4M tokens, Redwood provides a $2k pilot credit, unit price displayed in workbook (approx $18/1M with credit applied). No long-term commit.
2) Pilot + Commitment: 3–4M pilot then 12‑month Dedicated commit with step-down pricing to ~$12/1M once commit and quantization profile agreed.
3) Proof-of-concept self-hosting guidance: if you want to evaluate open-model self-host economics we’ll provide an architecture and TCO notes (but longer time to value).

Action items (I’ll take these)
- Laura: confirm whether procurement needs a specific billing/legal flow (PO vs contract) — I put a HubSpot link in the email thread for the deal.
- Karthik: we’ll scope latency/throughput for the 12–18M token case and capture any caching opportunities to reduce unit cost.
- Ben: deliver the workbook with three scenario tabs (pilot, 12M steady, 18M steady) and a one-page comparison PDF. 

Please see attachments: redwood_cost_workbook_v3.xlsx and host_comparison_onepager.pdf. Happy to walk through the workbook on Thursday — Laura, can you propose a time?

Best,
Ben Carter
Director of Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0205
